nodes.name: POM-MOF Pt confinement
nodes.procedure: Liu et al. used polyoxometalates (POMs) with octahedral cavities and many coordination sites and acid sites as 'metal precursors' to confine the Pt atom, then subsequently used a metal-organic framework (MOF) with a pore size slightly larger than the POM to confine the combination of the two to ensure the spatial dispersion and stability of the single-atom catalytic sites.

nodes.name: Co-CMS preparation
nodes.procedure: Carbon molecular sieves (CMS) with an ordered porous structure can select size-matched Co-containing metal precursors and confine them within the pores, reducing the distance between metal precursors and the hydroxyl groups inside the pores and thus allowing hydroxyl groups inside the pores to function.

nodes.name: Cu/CuAu core-shell nanocrystals
nodes.procedure: Gao et al. first synthesized Cu nanocubes and subsequently added a controllable concentration of HAuCl4 as a glob precursor to this solution. Due to the presence of the Kirkendall effect, electrochemical replacement occurred between metallic copper and Au3+, synthesizing Cu/CuAu core-shell nanocrystals with ordered intermetallic single-atom alloy (ISAA) layers.

nodes.name: Fe/CDs@PPSNs precursors with carbonization
nodes.procedure: Fe3O4, polystyrene-b-poly(acrylic acid) (PS-b-PAA), and cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) are assembled together to form Fe3O4@PSNs precursors. The precursors were evenly distributed and successfully encapsulated within porous tunnels filled with PS-b-PAA/CTAB. Notably, the precursors still maintain good monodispersity after in situ high-temperature carbonization in a nitrogen flow.

nodes.name: TOS confined SACs
nodes.procedure: Gu et al. reported a universal synthetic strategy where the transition metal precursors were introduced into the confined space of T template-occupied mesoporous silica SBA-15 (TOS) through manual grinding, followed by calcination to yield a SAC in which single atoms were stabilized in the form of M-O-Si.

nodes.name: Ir in MnO2 vacancy
nodes.procedure: MnO2 with a lattice and porous structure confines the iridium (Ir) atom in a manganese (Mn) vacancy in the lattice; subsequently, Ir coordinates with the oxygen atom within this vacancy.

nodes.name: Pt@C12A7 by ion confinement
nodes.procedure: Ye et al. used nanoporous crystal 12CaO·7Al2O3 (C12A7) as a support and (PtCl4)2- as a metal precursor, which was confined in the surface cavity through electrostatic interaction. After reduction, the Pt@C12A7 single-atom catalyst was obtained.
